stemMd: Why did the team avoid claiming perfect accuracy from agreement?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Two readings can never be compared.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Shielding always changes the true room temperature dramatically.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Both sensors might share the same error.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The sensors measured different physical quantities.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Agreement necessarily means both sensors are broken.

explanationMd: Two instruments can agree while both deviate from the true value in the same direction. The passage explicitly preserves this possibility. Agreement tests consistency but is not a complete calibration against a known reference.

distractorRationale.e: A shared error is possible, not established.
distractorRationale.a: The comparison was useful for investigating placement.
distractorRationale.b: The passage does not make that claim.
